official.deadline_note: The scholarship itself has no separate deadline: it is decided automatically with the admission offer. The decision-relevant date is HKUST's Priority Round deadline of 25 November 2026 for 2027/28 applicants with international qualifications; applications are then reviewed on a rolling basis from 26 November 2026 onwards and the overall application deadline is 30 June 2027.
official.status_note: HKUST's online application system for the 2027/28 entry opened on 2 October 2026; the Priority Round deadline is 25 November 2026, rolling admissions run from 26 November 2026 onwards, offers are announced from late December 2026, and applications close on 30 June 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Successful awardees receive "a full tuition waiver, renewable" for the normal duration of study (subject to satisfactory academic performance). HKUST publishes the non-local undergraduate tuition fee the waiver covers as HKD 260,000 (~USD33,300) per academic year for 2027/28.
benefits: "A full tuition waiver, renewable" for the normal duration of study, subject to satisfactory academic performance
"Top-up scholarship may be offered by School/Program Office provided that the maximum limit of 'Full Tuition Fee + HK$65,000 allowance' p.a. is not exceeded"
No separate scholarship application: students are notified of the scholarship decision when they receive their offer of admission
Scholarship and financial aid support remains available separately through HKUST's Scholarships and Financial Aid Office
eligibility: "All undergraduate program applicants from underrepresented nationalities are automatically considered" - there is no separate scholarship application
Must be an applicant to an HKUST undergraduate programme with international qualifications (non-local applicant)

Fulfil the General Admissions Requirements, School/Program-specific Requirements, and English Language Admissions Requirements

Maintain satisfactory academic performance to keep the full tuition waiver renewable

application_method: Apply through the HKUST Online Application System (opened 2 October 2026 for 2027/28 entry) - no separate scholarship application exists
Meet the Priority Round deadline of 25 November 2026 for the earliest consideration; rolling review runs from 26 November 2026 onwards and applications close 30 June 2027
Admissions scholarships are considered automatically once the application is submitted; award details are released with the admission offer
official.application_route: Submit the HKUST undergraduate admission application online (create an account, complete the form, upload documents, pay the HK$600 fee); consideration for this scholarship is automatic with no separate form.
official.study_mode: Full-time (HKUST undergraduate curriculum: 4 years, minimum 120 credits; 5 years for the BEng/BSc & BBA Dual Degree Program in Technology and Management)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to non-local applicants with international qualifications; the scholarship targets applicants from nationalities HKUST describes as underrepresented. Local and non-local applicants are considered under different admissions schemes, and any change in local/non-local status after application can lead to revocation of offers.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the award targets non-local applicants (international-qualification holders) from underrepresented nationalities; local students are admitted through separate schemes such as JUPAS.
official.duration: Renewable for the normal duration of the undergraduate degree (4 years; 5 years for the Dual Degree Program in Technology and Management), subject to satisfactory academic performance
official.description: HKUST established the Global Learners Scholarship to support the University's strategic objective of enhancing the diversity of its student community. Students do not apply for it: all undergraduate programme applicants from underrepresented nationalities are automatically considered, and successful awardees receive a full tuition waiver, renewable for the normal duration of study subject to satisfactory academic performance.
official.english_requirement: HKUST's English Language Admissions Requirements: IELTS Academic overall band 6.0 (IELTS Academic for UKVI is also accepted), or TOEFL iBT total score 80 for tests taken prior to 21 January 2026 (the official brochure lists a separate requirement for tests taken from 21 January 2026 onwards), or qualifying school results such as GCE AS/A-Level English grade E, IGCSE/GCSE English (First/Second Language) grade 4/C or 5/B, or IB English A Language and Literature / English A Literature grade 4; full per-qualification table is published by HKUST.

applicant_utility.summary: This is an automatic, no-application scholarship: your HKUST undergraduate admission application is the entire scholarship application, so the only controllable deadline is the 25 November 2026 Priority Round. Awardees from underrepresented nationalities get their non-local tuition of HKD 260,000 per year waived for the whole degree, but you must still fund roughly HKD 86,000-116,000 a year for accommodation and living costs yourself. Aim to submit in the Priority Round because offers and scholarship decisions roll out from late December 2026, giving you maximum time to arrange a student visa, the HKD 20,000 acceptance deposit and off-campus housing.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A non-local applicant to an HKUST undergraduate programme whose nationality HKUST treats as underrepresented and who wants tuition covered for the full degree without managing a separate scholarship application.
application_readiness_checklist: Create your HKUST Online Application System account well before 25 November 2026 - referee and IB Coordinator/Career Counselor emails are only triggered after you submit, and HKUST recommends they respond within two weeks
Book or schedule your IELTS/TOEFL early so a valid score exists before you upload proof of English proficiency

Prepare the six required documents (ID/travel document, personal statement, Grade 10 onwards school reports, English proficiency proof, exam certificates and prizes, referee nomination) as PDFs small enough to upload
Have a Visa or Mastercard ready for the HKD 600 non-refundable application fee (AliPay and WeChat Pay are also accepted)
Choose up to TWO application choices deliberately and set your alternative-choice preference before submitting, because programme choices are final once the form is submitted
common_rejection_risks: A weak or incomplete admission application - the scholarship is decided with the offer, so failing to meet the General, Programme-specific or English Language Admissions Requirements removes both the offer and the waiver
Referee or IB Coordinator/Career Counselor emails that are never answered or land in spam, leaving the application unreviewable at the Priority Round

Applying with a nationality HKUST does not currently treat as underrepresented and then relying on this award instead of stacking other scholarships such as the University Admissions Scholarship for Other Qualifications Holders or BAAS
Declaring incorrect local/non-local status or nationality data, which HKUST says can lead to revoked offers and forfeited fees
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The waiver covers tuition only. Budget separately for university accommodation (about HKD 21,000-51,000 per residential year in the first year; roughly HKD 4,500-18,000 per month off-campus thereafter), personal/living expenses of about HKD 65,000 per academic year, plus the HKD 600 application fee, HKD 20,000 acceptance deposit for non-local students, flights and student visa costs.
document_audit: School reports must run from Grade 10 onwards - applicants who only upload final-year transcripts leave a required document missing
The personal statement and school reports must match the application form; inconsistencies between uploaded documents and declared data risk revocation under HKUST's accuracy rules
IB, GCE-AL/IAL, Cambridge Pre-U and Indian High School Examination candidates must nominate a coordinator/counselor for predicted grades in addition to the academic referee
Examination certificates are required if you already hold results - conditional/predicted-only files are insufficient for final verification
alerts: HKUST does not publish which nationalities count as underrepresented, so do not assume eligibility from your passport alone - check with HKUST (ugenquiry@ust.hk) before building financial plans around this award

The current official wording caps any School/Programme Office top-up at "Full Tuition Fee + HK$65,000 allowance" p.a. - this supersedes the older HK$60,000 figure that still circulates in some catalogue entries
Apply by 25 November 2026: after that date applications continue on a rolling basis but the strongest scholarship-consideration window is the Priority Round
English tests taken from 21 January 2026 onwards are assessed under a different published TOEFL threshold, so recent test-takers should verify their score against the current brochure wording
The top-up allowance is discretionary and programme-dependent - treat the base award as tuition-only when financing your studies
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One submission does everything: create an account in HKUST's online application system, complete the form, upload the required documents, pay the HKD 600 fee, and referees/counselors respond by email - scholarship consideration and the award decision then happen automatically alongside the admission offer.
